 India tour of New Zealand 2nd ODI 
 New Zealand 0 – 0 Live India Live Updated a minute ago New Zealand vs India LIVE, India Strike Early in 2nd ODI Cricket, Score and Wickets (NZ 92/5, 30 ov)
 Follow New Zealand vs India live cricket score, ball-by-ball commentary, wickets and scorecard from the 2nd ODI at Basin Reserve in Wellington on VAVEL.
 Coverage by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta Updated November 7, 2026, 5:25 am GMT ADVERTISEMENT
 Live Last update 05:25 GMT 05:24 GMT a minute ago 30 ov: New Zealand 92/5
 New Zealand are 92/5 after 30 overs, a run rate of 3.06. At the crease: Daryl Mitchell 43 (84) and Mitchell Santner 17 (23). Auqib Nabi has figures of 6-0-28-2.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 Follow VAVEL on Google 05:11 GMT 15 minutes ago 27.3 ov: New Zealand 82/5
 New Zealand are 82/5 after 27.3 overs, a run rate of 2.98. At the crease: Daryl Mitchell 35 (69) and Mitchell Santner 17 (23). Arshdeep Singh has figures of 6.3-1-14-0.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 05:05 GMT 20 minutes ago After 26.2 overs: New Zealand 79/5
 New Zealand are 79/5 after 26.2 overs, a run rate of 3.00. At the crease: Mitchell Santner 15 (19) and Daryl Mitchell 34 (66). Anshul Kamboj has figures of 6.2-0-21-1.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 04:42 GMT 44 minutes ago 21 ov: New Zealand reach 55/5
 New Zealand are 55/5 after 21 overs, a run rate of 2.61. At the crease: Daryl Mitchell 25 (52) and Mitchell Santner 1 (1). Axar Patel has figures of 2-0-6-0.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 04:34 GMT an hour ago 19.2 ov: WICKET! Tom Latham departs, New Zealand 53/4
 Tom Latham is out, caught by Naman Dhir off Gurnoor Brar for 7 from 22 balls. New Zealand are 53/4 after 19.2 overs.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 04:27 GMT an hour ago 18 ov: New Zealand reach 48/3
 New Zealand are 48/3 after 18 overs, a run rate of 2.66. At the crease: Daryl Mitchell 22 (44) and Tom Latham 5 (17). Gurnoor Brar has figures of 4-1-6-0.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 04:17 GMT an hour ago After 15 overs: New Zealand 44/3
 New Zealand are 44/3 after 15 overs, a run rate of 2.93. At the crease: Tom Latham 3 (13) and Daryl Mitchell 21 (30). Anshul Kamboj has figures of 4-0-14-1.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 04:12 GMT an hour ago 14 ov: New Zealand 43/3
 New Zealand are 43/3 after 14 overs, a run rate of 3.07. At the crease: Daryl Mitchell 20 (26) and Tom Latham 3 (11). Gurnoor Brar has figures of 2-0-5-0.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 03:51 GMT 2 hours ago 10 ov: New Zealand 29/3, end of the powerplay
 New Zealand are 29/3 after 10 overs, a run rate of 2.90. That is the end of the first powerplay. At the crease: Daryl Mitchell 10 (11) and Tom Latham 0 (2). Auqib Nabi has figures of 5-0-21-2.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 03:43 GMT 2 hours ago 8.4 ov: WICKET! Henry Nicholls departs, New Zealand 23/3
 Henry Nicholls is out, bowled by Anshul Kamboj for 11 from 26 balls (1 four). New Zealand are 23/3 after 8.4 overs.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 03:26 GMT 2 hours ago 5.4 ov: WICKET! Will Young goes for 6
 Will Young is out, caught by KL Rahul behind the stumps off Auqib Nabi for 6 from 17 balls (1 four). New Zealand are 11/2 after 5.4 overs.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 03:24 GMT 2 hours ago 5 ov: New Zealand reach 7/1
 New Zealand are 7/1 after 5 overs, a run rate of 1.40. At the crease: Henry Nicholls 5 (12) and Will Young 2 (13). Arshdeep Singh has figures of 3-1-3-0.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 03:09 GMT 2 hours ago 1.5 ov: WICKET! Tim Seifert departs, New Zealand 0/1
 Tim Seifert is out, caught by Anshul Kamboj off Auqib Nabi for 0 from 5 balls. New Zealand are 0/1 after 1.5 overs.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 03:02 GMT 2 hours ago Play is under way: New Zealand are batting
 We are under way at Hnry Stadium, Wellington. Will Young and Tim Seifert are at the crease, with Arshdeep Singh bowling. New Zealand are 0/0 after 0.1 overs.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 02:41 GMT 3 hours ago Confirmed playing XIs
 Here are the two teams for today's match.
 New Zealand: Will Young, Tim Seifert, Henry Nicholls, Daryl Mitchell, Tom Latham, Glenn Phillips, Mitchell Santner (c), Nathan Smith, Kyle Jamieson, Jacob Duffy, Blair Tickner.
 India: Rohit Sharma, Shubman Gill (c), Virat Kohli, Shreyas Iyer, Axar Patel, KL Rahul, Naman Dhir, Anshul Kamboj, Arshdeep Singh, Auqib Nabi, Gurnoor Brar.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 02:39 GMT 3 hours ago Toss: India win the toss and choose to bowl first
 India have won the toss and elected to bowl first at Hnry Stadium, Wellington. That means New Zealand will bat first.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 02:12 GMT 3 hours ago Wellington weather watch: Wet outfield delay continues past scheduled 3:00 PM start
 Past 3:10 PM local time in Wellington, the coin toss and opening ball of the 2nd ODI between New Zealand and India remain on hold due to a wet outfield at Hnry Stadium .
 Super-soppers and ground crew continue drying the outfield so the umpires can set an official toss time without losing overs from the 50-over contest. We will bring you the coin toss and confirmed Playing XIs immediately once announced.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 01:48 GMT 4 hours ago 15 minutes to play at Hnry Stadium, Wellington: New Zealand vs India
 15 minutes remain until the opening over between New Zealand and India at Hnry Stadium, Wellington . Official session schedule: 15.00 start, First Session 15.00-18.30, Interval 18.30-19.00, Second Session 19.00-22.30 .
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 01:41 GMT 4 hours ago Weather update from Wellington: Toss delayed due to a wet outfield
 Official update from Hnry Stadium, Wellington: Match officials have confirmed that the coin toss and start of the 2nd ODI between New Zealand and India are currently delayed by a wet outfield .
 Ground staff are working on the damp patches across the outfield ahead of the umpires pitch and outfield inspection, with no overs lost at this stage of the scheduled 50-over day/night contest. Stay tuned right here for the inspection time, toss call and confirmed Playing XIs.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 01:28 GMT 4 hours ago 30 minutes to first ball: toss approaching for New Zealand vs India (2nd ODI)
 We are 30 minutes away from the scheduled start of New Zealand vs India in the 2nd ODI at Hnry Stadium, Wellington (ODI no. 5060). The captains are due out shortly for the coin toss and confirmed playing XIs.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 01:20 GMT 4 hours ago Countdown to the toss at 01:30 GMT and first ball at 02:00 GMT in Wellington
 Both squads are arriving at Hnry Stadium in Wellington as New Zealand attempt to level the three-match series at 1-1 against Shubman Gill's India.
 Live toss coverage and confirmed Playing XIs begin 30 minutes before the 02:00 GMT start, followed by uninterrupted over-by-over updates and full scorecard stats.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 01:20 GMT 4 hours ago Key individual battle: Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma against Kyle Jamieson's bounce
 Kyle Jamieson's high release point and extra bounce off a good length against Rohit Sharma, Shubman Gill and Virat Kohli headlines the opening 10-over powerplay.
 At the other end, Arshdeep Singh's left-arm swing back into New Zealand's top three poses an immediate test for Will Young and Tim Seifert.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 01:20 GMT 4 hours ago Middle-overs spin duel: Mitchell Santner and Glenn Phillips vs Axar Patel
 Controlling run-rate between overs 11 and 40 will hinge on left-arm orthodox spinners Mitchell Santner and Axar Patel, supported by Glenn Phillips' off-breaks.
 Dot-ball pressure through the middle phase proved decisive in restricting New Zealand to 185 in the series opener.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 00:51 GMT 5 hours ago Pace bowling battle: Arshdeep Singh and Kamboj vs Kyle Jamieson and Jacob Duffy
 With Wellington's coastal breeze regularly assisting swing and seam with the two new white Kookaburra balls, both pace attacks carry major wicket-taking threat.
 India utilized Arshdeep Singh, Anshul Kamboj, Auqib Nabi and Gurnoor Brar alongside Axar Patel's left-arm spin in the 1st ODI, while New Zealand counter with towering quick Kyle Jamieson, Jacob Duffy, Blair Tickner and Nathan Smith.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 00:42 GMT 5 hours ago Toss and Playing XI countdown in Wellington: Less than an hour to captains call
 With local time approaching 1:45 PM in Wellington, the official coin toss and confirmed Playing XIs at Hnry Stadium (33,500 capacity) are less than 50 minutes away ahead of the 3:00 PM NZDT (02:00 UTC) first ball.
 India hold a 1-0 advantage in the three-match ODI series on their 2026/27 tour of New Zealand, while the Black Caps look to level the series on home turf before the decider. Stay tuned here for the toss result and confirmed XIs as soon as they are announced.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 00:07 GMT 5 hours ago Hnry Stadium Wellington dimensions and pitch conditions
 Wellington's drop-in surface typically offers true bounce and brisk carry early on, rewarding batters who play late square of the wicket once the initial new-ball movement settles.
 Captains winning the toss under day/night lights in Wellington closely weigh overhead cloud cover and wind direction before choosing whether to bowl or bat first.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 6 Nov 23:24 GMT 6 hours ago 2nd ODI start time, Wellington venue and match format
 Today's day/night 50-over contest takes place at Hnry Stadium in Wellington, starting at 3:00 PM local New Zealand time (02:00 GMT / 7:30 AM IST).
 The official coin toss and confirmed Playing XIs from captains Mitchell Santner and Shubman Gill will be announced 30 minutes before the first delivery.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 6 Nov 23:00 GMT 6 hours ago Series recap: India lead 1-0 after 5-wicket DLS win in Auckland
 Shubman Gill's India hold a 1-0 series advantage after bowling New Zealand out for 185 in 40.2 overs at Eden Park in Auckland and chasing down the revised target at 143/5 in 22.4 overs (winning by 5 wickets with 56 balls remaining via DLS).
 A victory today in Wellington seals the ODI series for India with a game to spare, while the Black Caps must win to force a decider.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 6 Nov 23:00 GMT 6 hours ago India batting core: Rohit Sharma, Shubman Gill, Virat Kohli and KL Rahul
 India's top and middle order brings formidable ODI pedigree into Wellington, led by Rohit Sharma, captain Shubman Gill, Virat Kohli, Shreyas Iyer, KL Rahul, Axar Patel and Naman Dhir.
 India's aggressive powerplay scoring put immediate pressure on New Zealand's seamers in the Auckland opener.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 6 Nov 23:00 GMT 6 hours ago New Zealand response: Mitchell Santner's Black Caps eye Wellington leveller
 Skipper Mitchell Santner leads a Black Caps unit featuring Will Young, Tim Seifert, Henry Nicholls, Daryl Mitchell, Tom Latham and Glenn Phillips in the batting department.
 Building deeper middle-overs partnerships after losing all 10 wickets in 40.2 overs in the 1st ODI is New Zealand's top priority today.
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta
 6 Nov 23:00 GMT 6 hours ago Welcome to New Zealand vs India 2nd ODI live from Wellington
 Welcome to VAVEL's live ball-by-ball coverage of the 2nd One-Day International between New Zealand and India at Hnry Stadium in Wellington (ODI no. 5060).
 India lead the three-match series 1-0 heading into Wellington, with first ball scheduled for 02:00 GMT (3:00 PM NZDT / 7:30 AM IST).
 Live updates by Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta

 Jhonatan Andrés Martínez Cuesta has been director of VAVEL's Colombia edition since 2018. He joined VAVEL in 2014 as a writer and worked as a coordinator before taking charge of the edition. Based in Medellín, he covers Colombian football — especially the Antioquia clubs and Independiente Medellín — as well as international and women's football, cycling and other sports, and has covered thousands of matches live for VAVEL's Colombia, Mexico and US editions.
